issues.description: import-notation 'url' branch returns early when url() is present, potentially skipping required validation.
issues.detail: When primary is 'url' and params contain url(), the guard exits without examination. Reviewers question whether 'url() present implies no diagnostic needed' actually holds — malformed or mixed params may still need flagging. The asymmetric gating direction versus sibling branches is undocumented and risks silent under-validation.

issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex omits /i flag while sibling HAS_KEYWORD includes it, creating undocumented asymmetry.
issues.detail: In keyframe-selector-notation, the two pre-filter regexes disagree on case sensitivity without stated justification. Selectors like FROM/TO are case-insensitive in CSS, so the asymmetry risks false negatives or at minimum signals the data was not examined carefully. Normalize the flags or document the invariant.

issues.description: Font-weight pre-filter regexes encode weaker postconditions than the parser and lack documented over-approximation contract.
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED/HAS_NUMERIC match on full decl.value with \b boundaries, which can match inside var()/calc() fallbacks or mixed values like '400 bold'. The fast-path must over-approximate the slow-path matcher; this invariant is unstated. Mixed-value cases and the case-sensitivity inconsistency between HAS_NAMED and HAS_NUMERIC need a documented contract.

issues.description: selectorRegex = /./ sentinel for 'match everything' is clever where undefined or branching would be clearer.
issues.detail: walkRules accepts an absent filter for the same effect. Using /./ leaks implementation detail and makes intent harder to read. Branch on filter presence and call walkRules with or without a filter — same machine code, clearer diff for the next maintainer.

issues.description: Pre-filter regexes built from keyword sets without literal-escaping; safe today, fragile tomorrow.
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED, HAS_NUMERIC, HAS_PERCENTAGE, HAS_KEYWORD interpolate Set/Map contents directly into RegExp source. Current contents are alphanumeric/percent so it works, but if a future keyword contains a regex metacharacter the pattern silently corrupts. Add an escapeRegExp helper or document the precondition that all keywords are [a-z0-9%]+.

issues.description: Performance claim is unmeasured; no benchmark numbers and no regression tests pinning fast-path boundaries.
issues.detail: The PR touches six rules for performance but cites no before/after measurements, and no new tests assert that early-exit branches preserve diagnostic output for boundary cases. A small benchmark table and targeted tests per rule would convert this from tested-not-proved to demonstrated.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR is a sound performance optimization that adds cheap pre-filter regex checks before expensive parser passes across six *-notation rules. Two correctness concerns dominate: the import-notation 'url' branch inverts gating direction and may skip valid checks, and HAS_PERCENTAGE/HAS_KEYWORD in keyframe-selector-notation disagree on case-insensitivity without justification. The emerging pattern — a fast-reject filter that must over-approximate the slow-path matcher — is implemented inline six times with no shared abstraction or documented invariant. Recommend fixing the case-flag asymmetry, verifying the import-notation url gate, replacing the /./ sentinel with explicit branching, and adding benchmark numbers plus boundary tests before merge.
